payout_quote: Pay rate is $12.00 per hour - Alternate Judges & Clerks. Pay rate is $14.00 per hour - Judges - during Primary Election on ED - $12.00 an hour. In-person training: $8.00 an hour.
steps: Fill out the Brazoria County Election Worker Application on the county clerk's Poll Workers page and submit it; for Primary Elections select a political party preference (the application is forwarded to the selected county chair).
Attend training in Angleton (in-person training is paid at $8.00 an hour).
Work the full Election Day: setup at 6:00 AM, voting 7 AM-7 PM, then up to 2 hours of teardown and packing supplies.
Student poll workers may also apply with parent and school-principal permission forms.
catches: Pay is hourly, so the total depends on hours actually worked; the county states only the hourly rate plus the expectation of a 14-15-hour day.
Judges earn $14.00/hr in general elections but only $12.00/hr on Election Day in a Primary Election.
In-person training is paid at a lower $8.00/hr rate.
Workers must be able to work a 14-15-hour day and lift up to 35 lbs during setup/teardown.
biggest_catch: Hourly pay on a 14-15-hour day: $12/hr alternate judges and clerks ($168-$180/day), $14/hr judges ($196-$210/day) in general elections; judges drop to $12/hr on Primary Election Day; training is only $8/hr.
eligibility: Registered voter in Brazoria County; transportation; able to attend training in Angleton; able to assist in setup and packing up voting equipment including lifting up to 35 lbs; able to work a 14-15-hour day; cannot be an elected official, a candidate on the ballot, or employed by/related within the second degree to an opposed candidate on the ballot. Student poll workers need parent and school-principal permission.
timing: A typical election day starts with setting up the polling place at 6:00 AM, voting from 7 AM - 7 PM, and then taking down the voting equipment and packing up supplies for up to 2 hours. Workers must be able to work a 14-15-hour day.

notes: Brazoria County, Texas poll workers via the County Clerk's official page. Hourly rates: $12.00/hr alternate judges & clerks, $14.00/hr judges ($12.00/hr judges on Primary Election Day), in-person training $8.00/hr. Typical Election Day: 6:00 AM setup, 7 AM-7 PM voting, up to 2 hours teardown; 14-15-hour day expected ($168-$210/day depending on role and hours).
payout_value_note: Hourly rates ($12/hr alternate judges & clerks; $14/hr judges, $12/hr on Primary Election Day); per-day totals derived from the county's stated 14-15-hour day ($168 = 14h x $12; $210 = 15h x $14); in-person training at $8/hr.
numeric_basis: County requires workers able to work a 14-15-hour day (840-900 minutes); typical day: 6:00 AM setup, voting 7 AM-7 PM, up to 2 hours teardown.
